title: Stroke in the hospital: ischemic, hemorrhage or TIA
question: From this hospital discharge summary, assign the ICD-10-CM code for the cerebrovascular event (only that code).
note:
Admission Date: 05/12/2026
Discharge Date: 05/18/2026
Reason for Admission: Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage

Hospital Course:
The patient is a 78-year-old woman who presented to the emergency department with acute neurological symptoms. Imaging confirmed a nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage. She was admitted for conservative medical management, including blood pressure stabilization and close neurological monitoring. During her stay, she remained hemodynamically stable. The patient showed significant improvement over the course of the hospitalization. All neurological deficits were fully resolved prior to her discharge. She was able to participate in physical therapy and successfully met all criteria for safe discharge to her home.

Discharge Diagnoses:
1. Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage

Discharge Medications:
1. Lisinopril 10mg daily
2. Atorvastatin 40mg daily

Follow-up:
The patient is instructed to follow up with her primary care physician in one week and with neurology in two weeks for continued monitoring.

Electronically signed, L. Moreau, MD, 05/18/2026
explanations: Nontraumatic intracerebral hemorrhage, location not named: I61.9 (HCC 248).

distractors.why: It is a hemorrhage, not an infarction.
